name: Advaita Chandra
tagline: Learning in public, one question at a time.
photoAlt: Placeholder illustration standing in for a profile photograph.
bio: I'm Advaita — a student with a long-running interest in philosophy, Indian politics, technology, and data. This site is where I share what I'm researching and building. I'm not presenting myself as an expert; I'm documenting the process of learning, questioning, and improving.
learningDirection: Right now I'm working on two things: getting more rigorous about how I handle sources that disagree with each other, and getting better at building the tools I want to use. The data-visualisation and writing projects on this site came out of the first; the site itself came out of the second.

approach.title: Ask better questions
approach.detail: A vague question produces a vague answer. Most of the work happens before the research starts — narrowing a question until it is specific enough to be answered, and honest enough to admit what it excludes.

approach.title: Examine evidence
approach.detail: Find out where a number or claim actually came from. When sources disagree, record the disagreement rather than picking whichever figure is most convenient.

approach.title: Understand context
approach.detail: A fact without its context is easy to misuse. Definitions, time periods and methods of counting change what a figure means, so they belong alongside it.

approach.title: Explain clearly
approach.detail: If I cannot explain something plainly, I probably do not understand it yet. Writing is the test, not the write-up.

epistemicNote: Across this site I try to keep four things visually distinct: what a source says, what I infer from it, what I simply think, and what I do not know. Where you see a labelled block, that is what it is doing.
